findings.reason: Verified in topic_embed.rb that the raw embed_url is interpolated unescaped into an <a href> tag, and raw_html posts skip sanitising, so a single-quote-injected query string from an anonymous request yields a real stored XSS attribute.

Verified that the throttle and the TopicEmbed uniqueness check both key on the full URL, so each new query string bypasses the 60-second throttle and creates a new topic with a remote fetch, with no per-client limit.

Confirmed i.content is nil for feeds without content:encoded, so nil.scrub raises NoMethodError and aborts the poll loop, and TopicRetriever calls PollFeed inline, so the RetrieveTopic job also fails.

The `<%- end if %>` construct is fragile, but Erubis's newline handling likely makes the next output statement the modifier condition, which is truthy, so the template probably renders correctly; the failure is hedged with no concrete failing output.
The spec does depend on inline job execution in tests, but it is a test-quality concern on a non-critical path with no specific defect it would catch.

Verified the diff removed --category and created_at from the Disqus import, so imported threads lose their category and date, and import_remote adds a live fetch with no rescue; a silent undocumented regression in the tool.
The indexOf origin check is a real prefix-match weakness, but the handler only resizes the iframe, so the impact is minimal.
Verified force: true was added to an existing migration and the new topic_embeds migration; data loss only occurs in an unusual state where the table exists without its migration record.
A nil embed.post would make PostRevisor.new(nil) fail, which is real, but it requires a hard-deleted post, which is an uncommon path in Discourse that usually soft-deletes.
